newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds stay resilient to wobbly U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds stay resilient to wobbly U.S..

text.p: *Australian bonds remained underpinned by current positive fundamentals and attempted to decouple from the plight of the U.S. market going into its quarterly refunding auctions.
*Main local focus stays on Thursday's labour force data.
Australian bonds remained underpinned by current positive fundamentals and attempted to decouple from the plight of the U.S. market going into its quarterly refunding auctions.

The U.S. market faces the first of its three auctions totalling US$38 billion starting with the offer of US$16 billion of three-year notes later on Tuesday and comes at a time when the market is again the propects for monetary policy.
While local yields are some 15 basis points above the intra-day lows seen late last week, U.S. yields have steepened more sharply in the wake of Friday's strong data.
However, local activity was fairly subdued after an initial burst of activity on the futures floor on its reopening after Monday's bank holiday in the New South Wales state.

Traders said that domestic institutions are already finding themselves short of stock after the recent strong rally which had taken the long end of the curve to yield levels not seen since the early 1970s and were unwilling to go even shorter in the wake of the U.S. sell-off.
The reaction to the U.S. auction may give some guidance to domestic bonds in the next couple of days, but the main local focus remains on Thursday's labour force report for July.
Ten-year bonds outperformed against the U.S., putting support at 25 basis points under severe pressure and the lowest level since the early 1980s. The Canadian bond market was closed on Monday.
